description: Reframe LLD/java-cheatsheet.md from a 'Python -> Java translation reference' into 'Java specifics for LLD rounds' — the interview-minimal Java a candidate needs, organized by WHY each thing matters in a round. Demote the Python->Java mapping to one small callout. Per the workflow scope-addition notification, which REPLACES the earlier 'only add an @Autowired note' instruction. Independent of the other features (distinct file).
steps: Read LLD/java-cheatsheet.md fully first. Preserve the front-matter but UPDATE title/description to the new framing ('Java specifics for LLD rounds'). The page is already Java; this is a reorganization + reframe, not a Python->Java conversion.

Demote the current 'Mental model: Python -> Java' table to a SMALL 'Coming from Python, watch out for these' callout (a short admonition or a compact few-row table): duck typing -> static types; None -> null; no native method overloading; indentation -> braces. This is the ONLY remaining Python content and must NOT be the spine of the page.

Reorganize the body by WHY each thing matters: (1) Constructs used in every LLD answer — interface vs abstract class (implements = many, extends = one); enum for fixed states/types (with fields/methods, preferred over string constants); constructor injection + a short @Autowired explanation (Spring container creates the bean and injects it so the class never calls `new`; constructor injection preferred over field injection; this is DIP in practice); access modifiers (private fields, public API). (2) Collections you'll declare — List/Map/Set by interface (List<X> x = new ArrayList<>()); bug-preventing Map idioms getOrDefault/putIfAbsent/computeIfAbsent; when Deque/Queue/PriorityQueue; concurrent variants (ConcurrentHashMap, BlockingQueue) with a CROSS-LINK to LLD/concurrency.md (don't duplicate). (3) Gotchas that get you dinged — equals()+hashCode() together for Map/Set keys (or record); == vs .equals(); record for immutable value objects; final for constants/immutability; Optional instead of returning null. (4) Concurrency primitives (brief) — synchronized vs ReentrantLock, AtomicInteger; short, CROSS-LINK to LLD/concurrency.md, don't duplicate. (5) A tiny runnable skeleton — public static void main driving an in-memory demo (the 'working code' deliverable).

Keep the existing 'don't embarrass yourself' quick list. Trim streams & lambdas to a 2-line mention AT MOST (do not add Java surface area the user doesn't need). All code examples remain simple and tagged ```java. Keep the existing 'Related' cross-links and ensure they resolve.
Run the strict build; confirm no new WARNING and all cross-links resolve. Commit locally on branch lld-java (e.g. `docs(LLD): reframe java-cheatsheet to Java specifics for LLD rounds`). Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: Front-matter title/description reflect 'Java specifics for LLD rounds'.
The Python->Java mapping is reduced to ONE small callout (admonition or compact table) and is no longer the page spine; streams & lambdas are at most a 2-line mention.

The page is organized into the five WHY-based sections above and retains the 'don't embarrass yourself' list; concurrent collections and concurrency primitives cross-link to LLD/concurrency.md rather than duplicating it.

A short @Autowired / constructor-injection explanation is present and consistent with the roadmap DIP note (container creates+injects the bean; constructor injection preferred over field injection; DIP in practice).
`cd <worktree> && DISABLE_MKDOCS_2_WARNING=true python -m mkdocs build --strict` exits 0 with no NEW WARNING and all java-cheatsheet cross-links resolve.
